advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Scope the new CAS-mismatch WARNING to the renew/steal (lease-moved) path, or reword it so it does not falsely assert "lease moved" for acquire (lock-already-held) and release (idempotent) CAS mismatches.
evidence: _ref_lock.py:786-791 logs `"ref-lock: push to %s %s classified as CAS mismatch (lease moved) — stderr: %s"` unconditionally in the CAS branch

_push_lease_cas is reached from acquire via `_push_cas(repo_root, ref, oid, _ZERO_OID, remote)` (line 461) where a mismatch means create-only CAS rejected = lock already held, already logged at INFO: `"ref-lock acquire failed: %s already held (create-only CAS rejected)"` (line 464)
release reaches it via `_push_delete_cas` (line 490/812) where a mismatch is documented as "a benign idempotent success" and logged at INFO (line 503)
The bug context (renew -> LeaseLostError -> pass abort) only applies to the renew/steal advance path, not to acquire/release.
advisory.finding: The new WARNING log in the CAS-mismatch branch hardcodes "classified as CAS mismatch (lease moved)", but `_push_lease_cas` is shared by acquire (create-only CAS = "lock already held", a normal outcome), release (delete CAS = benign idempotent success), renew and steal. For acquire and release the lease did NOT move, so the message is inaccurate and elevates an expected/benign outcome to WARNING-level noise (acquire already logs this at INFO on line 464; release on line 503).
advisory.suggested_fix: Either pass a caller-supplied context/verb into `_push_lease_cas` so the log distinguishes "lock already held" / "idempotent release" from "lease moved", or reword the message to a neutral "remote CAS mismatch" and let the caller (renew) own the "lease moved" wording where it raises LeaseLostError.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a case driving a bare broad rejection stderr ('! [remote rejected] ...' / 'cannot lock ref ...') with no non-cas marker and no 'stale info', asserting the intended residual verdict so the `_is_cas_mismatch_stderr` fallthrough branch is covered.
evidence: src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/_ref_lock.py:756-760 `if _LEASE_MISMATCH_MARKER in stderr: return True` ... `if any(m in stderr for m in _NON_CAS_REJECT_MARKERS): return False` ... `return any(m in stderr for m in _PUSH_REJECT_MARKERS)`

NON_CAS fixtures each embed a non-cas marker ('File exists', 'internal server error', 'pre-receive hook declined', 'secondary rate limit'), and CAS_MISMATCH embeds 'stale info' — none is a bare 'rejected'/'cannot lock ref' with no other identifying phrase, so the fallthrough `return any(...)` branch is never taken under test.

ABSENCE: no test case drives a stderr like '! [remote rejected] refs/reconciler/lock' or 'error: cannot lock ref ...' with no accompanying non-cas cause and no 'stale info', which is the exact residual case the diff keeps classified as a CAS mismatch.
advisory.finding: The residual classification path of `_is_cas_mismatch_stderr` — a bare broad rejection marker ('! [rejected]' / 'cannot lock ref') with NO `_NON_CAS_REJECT_MARKERS` cause and NO 'stale info' — which still returns True (CAS mismatch) via the final `return any(m in stderr for m in _PUSH_REJECT_MARKERS)`, is not exercised by any test. Every NON_CAS fixture contains a non-cas marker and CAS_MISMATCH contains 'stale info', so the third, ambiguity-boundary branch the diff introduces has no coverage; a regression flipping this residual verdict would not be caught.
scenarios: A future edit tightens or drops the `_PUSH_REJECT_MARKERS` fallthrough (e.g. requires 'stale info' only), silently changing the residual-rejection verdict from cas-mismatch to fail-closed with no failing test.
git emits a bare '! [rejected]' with no diagnostic tail and the classifier's intended (documented) verdict is unverified.
advisory.suggested_fix: Add a fixture such as RESIDUAL = '! [remote rejected] refs/reconciler/lock (unknown reason)' and assert `_classify(monkeypatch, RESIDUAL) == "cas-mismatch"` (the documented fail-closed-on-ambiguity default), so the third branch of `_is_cas_mismatch_stderr` is exercised and a change to the fallthrough goes RED.
